activity_context.topic_title: The Parametric Equations of a Plane

feedback.problem:
Find a normal vector to the plane

$$
r=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+s[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,t,\,s\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
From the parametric equation, we have that $v=⟨-5,1,1⟩$ and $w=⟨3,1,-2⟩$ are parallel to the plane.

Now, we need to find a normal vector of the plane. To do that, we use the cross product of $v$ and $w$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =v\times w \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\times [\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -5 & 1 & 1 \\ 3 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =-3i-7j-8k \\  & =⟨-3,-7,-8⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the plane is $n=⟨-3,-7,-8⟩.$
